title: 짐작하고, 다짐하고, 시키기: 올걸 / 해야지 / 해라
objective: By the end, you can choose -을걸, -어야지, or -어라 to fit the situation and build each form correctly, including past guesses (-었을걸) and 하다 verbs (해야지, 해라).
summary: This worksheet compares three sentence endings: -을걸 for a guess, -어야지 for a promise or what should be done, and -어라 for a plain command.

task.title: Guess, promise, or command
task.line: Read each situation, then write or choose the ending that fits it.

forms.when: After a verb or adjective stem ending in a consonant (not ㄹ). Add 요 to be polite.
forms.means: A soft guess: "I think…, probably…" Often used to tell someone something they may not know.
forms.exampleMeaning: If we go now, there probably won't be any seats.

forms.when: After a stem ending in a vowel. A ㄹ stem only adds 걸 (살다 → 살걸). A noun + 이다 becomes N일걸 (학생일걸).
forms.exampleMeaning: The subway is probably faster than the bus.

forms.when: Past stem + -을걸. Use it when you guess that something has already happened.
forms.exampleMeaning: The meeting has probably already ended.

forms.when: After a verb stem, often when you are talking to yourself. ㅏ/ㅗ stems take -아야지, other stems take -어야지, and 하다 becomes 해야지.
forms.means: Your own decision: "I'm going to…, I must…"
forms.exampleMeaning: From tomorrow, I'm definitely going to get up early.

forms.when: When you speak to another person. 야죠 is the short spoken form.
forms.means: What the person should do, or what is natural: "You should…, of course you should…"
forms.exampleMeaning: If you have a cold, you should get plenty of rest.

forms.when: After a verb stem, when you speak to children, or to close friends your own age or younger. ㅏ/ㅗ stems take -아라, other stems take -어라, and 하다 becomes 해라.

watchOut: 먹을껄요 (X) → 먹을걸요 (O): It sounds like 껄, but you always write 걸.
벌써 출발할걸요 (X) → 벌써 출발했을걸요 (O): When you guess that something has already happened, use -었을걸.
To say "I think it will rain tomorrow": 내일 비가 와야지 (X) → 내일 비가 올걸 (O). Use -을걸 for a guess. -어야지 is for a decision or something that should happen.
할머니, 여기 앉아라 (X) → 할머니, 여기 앉으세요 (O): Use -어라 only with children, or with close friends your own age or younger. With elders and people you should be polite to, use -(으)세요.
공부하어라 (X) → 공부해라 (O): A 하다 verb becomes 해라 (하여라 in formal writing), never 하어라, and 해야지 follows the same rule.
exercises: Make a guess with -을걸요: ① 그 식당은 점심시간에 사람이 (많다) ____. ② 지민 씨는 아직 부산에 (살다) ____. ③ 준호 씨 동생은 아직 (대학생이다) ____. ④ 수진 씨는 어제 고향에 (도착하다) ____.
A parent is talking to a child. Change the word in ( ) with -어라: ① 밥 먹기 전에 손을 (씻다) ____. ② 내일 학교에 가야 하니까 일찍 (자다) ____. ③ 친구가 오기 전에 방 좀 (청소하다) ____.
You are talking to yourself after a late dinner. Choose the right ending: 내일부터는 밤에 라면을 안 (먹을걸 / 먹어야지 / 먹어라).
Your friend asks, "민호 지금 집에 있을까?" It is 5 p.m., and Minho usually works until 7. Choose the reply that makes a guess: ① 아직 회사에 있을걸. ② 아직 회사에 있어야지. ③ 아직 회사에 있어라.
Give advice with -어야지요: 동료: 요즘 너무 피곤해요. 나: 그럼 오늘은 일찍 집에 (들어가다) ____.
Put the words in order to make a promise to yourself: 운전면허를 / 따야지 / 내년에는 / 꼭
answers: ① 많을걸요 ② 살걸요 ③ 대학생일걸요 ④ 도착했을걸요
① 씻어라 ② 자라 ③ 청소해라
내년에는 꼭 운전면허를 따야지. (내년에는 운전면허를 꼭 따야지. / 운전면허를 내년에는 꼭 따야지. / 꼭 내년에는 운전면허를 따야지.)
